member.name: T:Graphs.Distance.Geodesic.FisherRaoSimplex
member.summary:
Fisher-Rao geodesic distance on the probability simplex (discrete probability mass vectors). Uses the Bhattacharyya-angle form: d = 2 * arccos(sum_i sqrt(p_i * q_i)) which is the exact geodesic on the statistical manifold of categorical distributions.
INPUT CONTRACT: each input must be a non-negative D-vector summing to 1 (a probability mass function). Typical uses: topic model outputs, LDA document-topic distributions, any discrete distribution embedding.
CONTRAST WITH FisherRaoHalfPlane: FisherRaoHalfPlane is the exact geodesic for continuous univariate Gaussian parameters [mu, log_sigma] on the Poincaré upper half-plane. Use FisherRaoSimplex for discrete PMFs; use FisherRaoHalfPlane for Gaussian parameter spaces (e.g. GaussianManifold generator).
LENGTH GUARD: explicit check for p.Length != q.Length — TensorPrimitives slices both spans to p.Length, so a shorter q would throw inside TensorPrimitives with an unhelpful bounds error rather than at the call boundary.
FUTURE — IStatisticalManifold: Both classes will implement IStatisticalManifold once multivariate or Dirichlet families are added (those require numerical geodesic integration over the FIM and need a shared interface).

member.name: F:Graphs.Distance.Geodesic.Poincare.BoundaryMargin
member.summary: Margin from the unit-ball boundary used by . Points with ‖x‖ ≥ 1 − BoundaryMargin are projected radially inward to that radius before the distance computation. Sized for acosh's numerical stability — 1e-5 gives the denominator (1 − ‖a‖²)(1 − ‖b‖²) roughly 2e-5 of headroom rather than the previous 1e-12 which was tight enough that the 1e9 sentinel path was hit frequently for plausible inputs.

member.name: M:Graphs.Distance.Geodesic.Poincare.Distance(System.Double[],System.Double[])
member.summary: Poincaré (hyperbolic) distance in the unit ball model. d(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2 · ‖u − v‖² / ((1 − ‖u‖²)(1 − ‖v‖²))). Assumes points lie inside the open unit ball; out-of-bounds points are projected radially to radius 1 − BoundaryMargin before the distance computation, producing a real (large but finite) Poincaré distance rather than a sentinel.
member.remarks: Explicit length guard: loop accumulates norms over a.Length iterations — a shorter b would silently under-accumulate without throwing.

member.name: T:Graphs.Distance.Other.Hamming
member.summary: 64-bit packed Hamming distance — XOR + POPCNT on a pair of ulongs. The fast path for callers that already hold bit-packed feature vectors (genome k-mer signatures, MinHash sketches, etc.). For the standard "count coordinates where labels differ" semantic over of double, use .

member.name: T:Graphs.Distance.Other.HammingMetric
member.summary: Symbol-Hamming distance over of double: counts coordinates where a[i] != b[i]. Matches the scikit-learn / scipy metric='hamming' semantic except that scipy normalizes to [0, 1] by dividing by length — this implementation returns the raw count for compositional cleanliness (kernels in this codebase scale to the bandwidth, not to a fixed range).

remarks.para: Symbol encoding. Each coordinate's value is treated as an opaque symbol identity — integer labels (0, 1, 2, …) stored in double slots is the standard idiom and what Blatt-style symbolic-sequence clustering expects (one coordinate per sequence position, value = amino-acid or DNA-base index, etc.). Real-valued inputs are compared bit-exactly via !=; for noisy real-valued inputs prefer a continuous metric (Euclidean, Manhattan) instead.

Why this replaced the bit-packing path. The previous implementation packed a[i] != 0 into bit i of a ulong, then XOR/POPCNT'd. That had two silent bugs: (1) dimensions > 64 wrapped (C# masks shift counts mod 64), so high coordinates collided rather than overflowed; (2) it preserved only whether each coordinate was zero or non-zero, so [1, 2, 3] and [5, 6, 7] hashed identical and got Hamming distance 0. The fast 64-bit path is preserved as for callers that already hold ulong-packed data.

member.name: T:Graphs.Distance.Other.NcdCompressor
member.summary: Compressor selection for NCD. All options are System.IO.Compression streaming compressors — no external dependencies. Brotli is the default; designed for text and ships with a static English/HTML/CSS dictionary that helps short-input compression. Deflate / GZip / ZLib are the calibration-clean alternatives (no static dictionary), differing only in stream framing overhead.

member.summary: Pairwise NCD between two byte payloads. Public entry point for non-graph consumers (e.g. per-segment text scoring in downstream tools).
